reason: While the Hebrew people in this text express fear and uncertainty—notably when they ask Moses to speak with them rather than God directly to avoid death (Exodus 19:19), and when they question Moses' whereabouts during the Golden Calf incident—there is no explicit blame directed at their leaders (Moses or Aaron) or at Yahweh for putting them at risk. Aaron explains the people's behavior as due to their own inclination toward evil, but the people themselves do not articulate blame for being placed in danger. The fear and anxiety are evident, but formal blame is not expressed.
